numerical_failure.observed_behavior: Rolling cov/corr over float64 series with a large shared offset (about 1e12) returns wrong values after a large value leaves the window; in the PR reproducer rolling(5).cov(y).iloc[4:7].tolist() gives [1.099968..., -0.300072..., -0.800026...]. Per the commit, ssqdm_x/ssqdm_y collapse to round-off once the dominating value leaves the window, and a negative ssqdm_x can reach the square root in calc_corr yielding NaN.
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: Exact cov values [1.1, -0.3, -0.8] for the reproducer windows iloc[4:7]; accumulators should stay accurate after a large value leaves the window and not produce NaN from a negative ssqdm_x.
trigger_conditions: Series carries a large shared offset (about 1e12 added to values)
A large value dominates ssqdm_x/ssqdm_y and then leaves the rolling window
Incremental cov/corr accumulators are used without recompute after cancellation
A negative ssqdm_x reaches the square root in calc_corr, producing NaN

numerical_characteristics.precision: rtol=1e-12 with atol=0 in one test; the incremental update is designed to hold to a tolerance named in a test comment, and the cancellation threshold is EpsF64 * 1e3 (InvCondTol)
numerical_characteristics.magnitude: Large shared offset around 1e12 (values like 1e12 and 1e7 leave the window), with large magnitudes such as 1e12 dominating the sums; anchor origin is capped at sqrt(float64 max) to avoid overflow
numerical_characteristics.tolerance: rtol=1e-12, atol=0 for the equality check; InvCondTol = EpsF64 * 1e3 for the cancellation test
category_specific_evidence: Reproducer from PR#66678: x and y are float64 series offset by 1e12; rolling(5).cov(y).iloc[4:7] returns about [1.099968, -0.300072, -0.800026] versus exact [1.1, -0.3, -0.8].
Commit GH#65739: after a large value leaves the window, ssqdm_x/ssqdm_y collapse to round-off, causing silently wrong results or NaN from a negative ssqdm_x reaching the square root in calc_corr.

Fix anchors accumulators to the first value in the window so a common offset cancels exactly; values large enough to overflow the subtraction are not used as anchors (MaxOriginMagnitude = sqrt(finfo(float64).max)).
Test test_rolling_cov_corr_outlier_exit_no_nan uses series with 1e12, 1e7 and -1e12 values, window 3, and checks no NaN after window-1 and results against numpy cov/corrcoef on re-centered chunks.
Test comment notes the rtol is the tolerance the incremental update is designed to hold to, not float64 noise, since some windows still contain 1e12.
cancellation_suspected compares ssqdm_xy, ssqdm_x, ssqdm_y and peak deviations; the non-abs comparisons catch negative ssqdm values from cancellation.
reproduction_risks: The exact expected values in the PR reproducer are given to only a few digits (1.1, -0.3, -0.8) and the tolerance used to judge them is not stated in the passages.
Results depend on window contents after large values exit, so reproduction must include the large-value exit step.
The 1e12 offset and the 1e7 value are the only magnitudes cited; behavior at other magnitudes is not stated.
